# Lebob

> Lebob is an independent, not-for-profit robotics team from Perth, Western
> Australia. It competes in FIRST Tech Challenge as team 29550 and in FIRST LEGO
> League as team 3236. Most members attend Perth Modern School, but Lebob is not a
> school team: it is a community team the students started and run themselves under
> Lebob Robotics, an unincorporated not-for-profit association with its own ABN. In
> the 2025/26 UNEARTHED season it won the FIRST LEGO League National Championship
> West at Curtin University and went on to the Korea Open Invitational in Jeonju,
> South Korea, where its innovation project SoftSense won a prize. Its current
> build is the 2026-27 FIRST Tech Challenge BIOBUZZ robot.

Everything the team produces is published. All eight competition documents from the
2025/26 season are readable in full as HTML on this site, alongside the original
PDFs, and the engineering work behind SoftSense is open source.

## Key facts

- Full name: Lebob. Also written Team Lebob and Lebob Robotics.
- Location: Perth, Western Australia, Australia.
- Organisation: Lebob Robotics, an unincorporated not-for-profit association started and run by the students. Lebob is NOT a school team and has no parent school, club or host organisation.
- School attended by members: most members attend Perth Modern School. This is where the students go to school, not who runs the team.
- Members: eight students, plus two mentors, Jade and Kaelie.
- FIRST Tech Challenge team number: 29550. Current season: BIOBUZZ, 2026-27.
- FIRST LEGO League team number: 3236.
- Korea Open Invitational 2026 entry code: KOI34.
- Contact: team@lebob.com.au
- ABN: 41 535 175 584. All sponsorships are invoiced under this ABN.

## Current season, 2026-27 FIRST Tech Challenge BIOBUZZ

- Programme: FIRST Tech Challenge, team 29550.
- Game: BIOBUZZ, 2026-27 season.
- Status: robot build and documentation in progress. Season material will be published on this site and in the Lebob-Robotics GitHub organisation as it is produced.

## Season results, 2025/26 UNEARTHED

- 30 November 2025, regional tournament, Aquinas College, Salter Point, Perth. Advanced to the National Championship.
- 13 December 2025, FIRST LEGO League National Championship West, Curtin University, Perth. Western Australian National Champions.
- 3 to 5 July 2026, FIRST LEGO League Korea Open Invitational, Jeonju National University of Education, Jeonju, South Korea. Prize for the SoftSense innovation project.

## Pages

- [About Lebob](https://lebob.com.au/about/): the definitive description of the team. Team numbers, roster, mentors, how the team is organised as an independent not-for-profit, the full results table, and how the team works.
- [SoftSense](https://lebob.com.au/projects/softsense/): the technical writeup of the innovation project. A self sensing soft gripper for ROV manipulator arms that reads grip force from motor current instead of a fingertip sensor. Fin Ray TPU fingers, a flooded printed drivetrain, crosshatch grip texture, materials, FEA campaigns, bench results and operating boundaries.
- [Documentation library](https://lebob.com.au/docs/): every document the team has produced, organised by season.
- [FLL 2025/26 UNEARTHED season](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/): all eight season documents, grouped by competition stage.
- [Media gallery](https://lebob.com.au/media/): photographs from the season.
- [Sponsors](https://lebob.com.au/sponsors/): the six Founding Supporters backing the team.
- [How to sponsor](https://lebob.com.au/sponsors/how-to/): five sponsorship tiers from $500, plus in kind support.

## Season documents, full text

- [Regionals Innovation Documentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/regionals-innovation-documentation/): the first innovation writeup. The underwater archaeology problem, the research behind it, and the CTD 4000 manipulator concept.
- [Nationals General Documentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/nationals-general-documentation/): fifteen weeks of session notes plus the post regionals run testing log.
- [Nationals Robot Design Journal](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/nationals-robot-design-journal/): mission strategy, five attachments, and the PyBricks code architecture.
- [Nationals Innovation Documentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/nationals-innovation-documentation/): four failure modes of industrial ROV grippers, the four part solution, and the move from titanium to printed plastic.
- [Internationals General Documentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/internationals-general-documentation/): six months of weekly engineering logs from January to June 2026, the robot run log, and the attendance record.
- [Internationals Robot Design Documentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/internationals-robot-design-documentation/): the 545 point run plan, seven attachments, the code, and the gearbox rebuild.
- [Internationals Innovation Documentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/internationals-innovation-documentation/): the full SoftSense engineering record, including the finger FEA campaign, the grip texture study, the motor study, the drivetrain limit, materials, the seawater audit and the readiness assessment.
- [Internationals Judging Presentation](https://lebob.com.au/docs/fll-2025-2026/internationals-presentation/): all 71 slides from the Korea Open judging deck, each with the text it carries.
